issue.body:
Closes #25365.

These changes fix the weird behavior described in #25365, by applying two simple changes:
- remove all entries of a buffer from the jump list when deleting it
- not adding a new entry to the jump list if the next buffer to be displayed was also found in the jump list

This makes the jump list behave exactly as you would expect when deleting buffers

issue.title: `Ctrl-^` behaves unintuitively when deleting buffers

repository.name: neovim
repository.description: Vim-fork focused on extensibility and usability

issue.body:
### Problem

This issue is similar to https://github.com/neovim/neovim/issues/25365, but for the `alternate-file`.

It often happens that when deleting a buffer (with `:bd`), say `file1`, that buffer is just unlisted and "invisibly" stays the `alternate-file` for another buffer `file2`. When `file2` is active, pressing `Ctrl-^` will make neovim attempt to re-open `file1`.

Problems:
- some buffers can't be reloaded
- typically, a buffer was deleted for a reason, so it's unlikely that someone would use the `Ctrl-^` command with the intention to reload that buffer (although in certain scenarios this could be a valid use case)

If instead one doesn't just delete the buffer, but wipes it with `:bw`, then doing `Ctrl-^` as above, one gets the error "E23: No alternate file".

### Expected behavior

I believe that for the vast majority of use-cases, it would be practical that when deleting/wiping a buffer, another buffer predictably becomes the alternate buffer. The most obvious candidate would be closest other listed buffer in the jumplist.

issue.body:
### Problem

This issue is similar to https://github.com/neovim/neovim/issues/25365, but for the `alternate-file`. I previously opened this as a "feature request" issue but was told it fits more the "bug report" issue.

It often happens that when deleting a buffer (with `:bd`), say `file1`, that buffer is just unlisted and "invisibly" stays the `alternate-file` for another buffer `file2`. When `file2` is active, pressing `Ctrl-^` will make neovim attempt to re-open `file1`.

Problems:
- some buffers can't be reloaded
- typically, a buffer was deleted for a reason, so it's unlikely that someone would use the `Ctrl-^` command with the intention to reload that buffer (although in certain scenarios this could be a valid use case)

If instead one doesn't just delete the buffer, but wipes it with `:bw`, then doing `Ctrl-^` as above, one gets the error "E23: No alternate file".

### Steps to reproduce

`nvim --clean file1`
`:e file2`
`:e file3`
Now, `file3` is active, and `file2` is the `alternate-file`.
`:bd2` to close `file2`, and the active buffer is still `file3`.
press `Ctrl-^`
Now, `file2` is loaded again even though it was just deleted.

### Expected behavior

I believe that for most use-cases, it would be practical that when deleting/wiping a buffer, another buffer predictably becomes the alternate buffer. The most obvious candidate would be closest other listed buffer in the `jumplist`.

### Neovim version (nvim -v)

NVIM v0.10.0-dev-2250+g6bba4bece

### Vim (not Nvim) behaves the same?

no, vim 8.2

### Operating system/version

Ubuntu 22.04

### Terminal name/version

konsole 23.08.4

### $TERM environment variable

tmux-256color

### Installation

appimage (nightly)

repository.name: neovim
repository.description: Vim-fork focused on extensibility and usability

issue.body:
### Problem

In v0.9.5, closing a buffer and then pressing `ctrl-o` re-opened the closed buffer. In v0.10.0, this is no longer the case, and `ctrl-o` jumps back to the previous position only in currently open buffers.

### Steps to reproduce

Assuming you have binaries for both v0.10.0 and v0.9.5 named `nvim-0.10.0` and `nvim-0.9.5` respectively:

```sh
nvim-0.9.5 --clean file1 file2
:bdelete
<C-o> # opens buffer that was just deleted
```

```sh
nvim-0.10.0 --clean file1 file2
:bdelete
<C-o> # does not open buffer that was just deleted
```

### Expected behavior

`<C-o>` should presumably behave as it did in 0.9.5, by opening deleted buffers

### Neovim version (nvim -v)

0.10.0 release, and latest prerelease 0e9c92a

### Vim (not Nvim) behaves the same?

Vim 9.1.400 does not have this issue

### Operating system/version

macOS 14.5

### Terminal name/version

Alacritty 0.13.2

### $TERM environment variable

tmux-256color

### Installation

Homebrew
